ruleset.name: jpinpoint-nextgen-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint "nextgen" rule set: new Kotlin remoting rules using PMD 7.28.0 type-resolution XPath functions (pmd-kotlin:typeIs, pmd-kotlin:matchesSig). These rules REQUIRE a PMD version that supports those features and therefore are NOT included in the standard jpinpoint-kotlin-rules.xml, to keep that file working on older PMD versions. See the "Nextgen rules" section in the README for details. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidExcessiveClassloadingWithSaajSoap
rule.message: Avoid excessive class loading with SAAJ SOAP messaging, use alternative Axiom, or system properties.
rule.description: Problem: SAAJ uses DOM to load the XML document in memory, which uses a TransformerFactory. The implementation class of it is loaded on every call that causes lock contention under load. This means long response times. Solution: If possible, use Axiom SOAP messaging which uses the faster StAX. If you have/want to stick to SAAJ, set the proper system properties to prevent the excessive class loading. Note: Axiom (2.0) is available again in Spring web services, since version 4.1. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath
property.value: (: Constructor call to SaajSoapMessageFactory without TransformerFactory system property fix :) //PostfixUnaryExpression[ pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('org.springframework.ws.soap.saaj.SaajSoapMessageFactory#<init>(*)') and not(ancestor::ClassBody//PostfixUnaryExpression[ PrimaryExpression/SimpleIdentifier/T-Identifier[@Text='System'] and PostfixUnarySuffix/NavigationSuffix/SimpleIdentifier/T-Identifier[@Text='setProperty'] and .//T-LineStrText[@Text='javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory'] ]) ] , (: Class-level property with explicit SaajSoapMessageFactory type (no constructor call, that is caught above). (: isWithin pattern :) pmd-kotlin:isWithin('function-body'/'lambda') does not exist in released PMD (7.28.0) - it is from a proposed/experimental future API. Replaced here with a plain ancestor:: check instead, since PropertyDeclaration is used for class-level properties, local variables and lambda-local variables alike; only the ancestor axis distinguishes a class-level declaration from a local one. If/when isWithin() is actually released, search for "(: isWithin pattern :)" to find and simplify all occurrences of this idiom. :) //PropertyDeclaration[ not(ancestor::FunctionBody or ancestor::LambdaLiteral) and pmd-kotlin:typeIs('org.springframework.ws.soap.saaj.SaajSoapMessageFactory') and not(.//PostfixUnaryExpression[pmd-kotlin:matchesSig('org.springframework.ws.soap.saaj.SaajSoapMessageFactory#<init>(*)')]) and not(ancestor::ClassBody//PostfixUnaryExpression[ PrimaryExpression/SimpleIdentifier/T-Identifier[@Text='System'] and PostfixUnarySuffix/NavigationSuffix/SimpleIdentifier/T-Identifier[@Text='setProperty'] and .//T-LineStrText[@Text='javax.xml.transform.TransformerFactory'] ]) ]
